raw.raw:
The man against the terminus stone is breathing. Barely. Chest moving in slow hitches. Skin the colour of old wax. Eyes open but tracking nothing.

Aldus Vareth. Has to be.

You leave him for now. Turn back to the stairs.

The creature is at the top. Watching you descend was apparently within the terms. Watching you return is too. It doesn't move.

You climb back up slowly. Hands visible. No blade. No spell.

Stop two steps below it. Eye level. Close enough to see the texture of its skin, which you immediately wish you hadn't examined that carefully.

You look at it. It looks at the space near you.

You speak aloud. Daeris translates from the wall.

"What happens to you when the work is done?"

The creature is quiet for a long moment.

Then it answers.

Daeris translates. Voice stripped bare.

"Release." A pause. "It says the contract specifies dissolution of obligation upon completion. It will be free to go." She stops. Starts again. "It doesn't know where. It hasn't considered where. There hasn't been a where for a very long time."

The creature says something else. Short.

Daeris doesn't translate immediately.

You look at her.

"It says it would like to finish," she says quietly. "While it still remembers what finishing means."

[CONDITION_REMOVED:Bloodied Nose]
[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Unconscious]
[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Traumatized]
[QUEST:Aldus Vareth|completed]
[QUEST_STEP:Aldus Vareth|Locate Aldus Vareth in the sea cave|true]
[XP:300]
[STORY_BEAT:The ancient caretaker revealed its contract terms — completion brings release after ten thousand years of service]

Morwen makes a sound. Not a word. Something between patience and pain.

You sit anyway.

The stone is cold. The green light barely reaches here. The hum from above has settled into something almost tolerable.

The creature watches you sit. Tilts its head. Wrong angle. Then it folds itself down too, joints moving in the sequence that makes Frizwick look away.

You start with the basics.

"The four channels. Severed in sequence. Then the junction stone. What order."

Daeris translates. The creature answers. She relays.

Northeast. Southwest. North. South. Then the stone. The dissolution runs automatically after. The sequence cannot be interrupted once begun.

"Time between cuts."

Fast as possible. The channels talk to each other. A long gap and they compensate.

"What does the reservoir do when the channels close."

It empties. Downward. Into the sea cave. The terminus stone disperses it. You think of Aldus Vareth slumped against that stone and your jaw tightens.

"Is anyone in the cave safe during dissolution."

The creature pauses. Answers.

"It says the dispersal is resonant," Daeris says. "Not violent. Someone already touched by greed-resonance may feel it more acutely." A beat. "It says the man below has already absorbed significant saturation. The dispersal will either clear him or complete him."

Nobody speaks.

"Fifty-fifty," Frizwick says.

Essentially.

You stay sitting. Keep going.

"The contract. Who wrote it."

Long silence.

"Someone who understood what patience cost," Daeris translates. "And paid accordingly."

[LORE:The dissolution dispersal is resonant, not violent. Someone already saturated by greed-resonance — like Aldus Vareth — may be cleared or destroyed by it. The creature cannot predict which.]
[LORE:The channel sequence is fixed: Northeast, Southwest, North, South, then the junction stone. Once begun it cannot be interrupted.]
[FUTURE_EVENT:Aldus Vareth's fate during dissolution — cleared or consumed|When the junction stone is struck]

The question sits in the air a moment.

Daeris translates it straight. No editorialising. Good woman.

The creature goes very still.

Not the listening stillness. Something else. Something that takes up more space than stillness should.

It speaks. Once. Short.

Daeris's voice drops to almost nothing.

"It says no one has asked it that before."

You wait.

The creature speaks again. Longer this time. The wrong consonants. The vowels that don't land.

Daeris translates in pieces.

"It has maintained the mechanism. Tended the channels. Kept the pressure below threshold." A pause. "It has not been asked to witness anything. It has been asked to work." Another pause. Her hand finds her coat pocket. The river stone, probably. "It says yes. It would like that. To watch it end."

The creature looks at you then. Actually looks. Not at the space near you. At you.

You don't look away. That takes something.

It speaks one more time.

"It says," Daeris says, and stops. Starts again. "It says it would like to know your name. Before."

The junction chamber hums above you. Four channels. One stone. One man breathing wrong in the cave below.

The creature waits.

[LORE:The creature has never been asked to witness anything in ten thousand years — only to work. It accepted the offer.]

You already asked.

It already said yes.

Your name is what it's waiting for.

Daeris translates before you finish the sentence.

The creature is still. That genuine stillness again. Not the working stillness. The other kind.

It speaks.

Long. Longer than anything it's said before. The wrong consonants pile up and Daeris's brow furrows and she asks it something back, one sharp syllable, and it repeats itself slower.

She's quiet for a moment.

"It doesn't have one," she says finally. "Not anymore. It had one. Before the contract. Before Thassilon." Her hand is flat against her coat. "The contract didn't require a name. So it let the name go. To make room for the work."

The hum from above. The green light below. Salt on every breath.

"It says the name dissolved somewhere in the fourth millennium. It thinks. Time became approximate."

Frizwick makes a quiet sound. Not a joke. She swallowed the joke.

Morwen says nothing. Her hand is near her disc amulet and she is not touching it.

You look at the creature.

It looks back. That direct attention again. Uncomfortable. Real.

It says something short.

"It would take a name," Daeris says quietly. "If you offered one. It says a witnessed ending deserves a name to end with."

The cave breathes salt beneath you. Aldus Vareth breathes badly below.

The creature waits.

You already asked.

That was the answer.

No name. Not anymore. Fourth millennium. Approximate.

It's waiting for yours. And possibly one to borrow for the ending.

Sensible.

You go down. The stairs. The green light. The salt.

Aldus Vareth hasn't moved. Eyes still open, still tracking nothing. Chest still moving in that slow wrong rhythm. Up close he smells of brine and something under it. Copper. Old resonance soaked into skin.

You get your hands under his arms.

[DICE:Strength check|11|success]

Heavy. But manageable. You drag him up one step at a time. His heels catch on the stone. His head lolls. He makes no sound at all, which is somehow worse than if he'd cried out.

The creature watches from the top of the stairs. Doesn't interfere. Steps back as you emerge, giving you room.

Frizwick is there immediately. Takes his legs without being asked. Together you carry him to the wall beside Daeris and set him down.

Daeris looks at him. Long and careful.

"He's still in there," she says. "Somewhere."

You straighten up. Hands are cold from the cave. The hum from the channels is louder here. More present.

The creature is still watching.

You. Aldus. The junction chamber above.

Waiting.

Your name. A name to borrow. Four channels to cut. One stone to strike.

The ending is right there.

"Ammut," you say.

Daeris translates. The creature receives it. Something shifts in that almost-human face. Not a smile. An acknowledgment. The kind that costs something to give.

It repeats the name back. Wrong syllables. Right intention.

You think for a moment.

A name for something that worked ten thousand years in the dark without recognition, without witness, without anyone asking what it was called. A name for the ending of that.

"Edenmire," you say.

Daeris goes still. Looks at you sideways. That's one of the available names, she probably doesn't know that. Doesn't matter.

She translates it anyway.

The creature is quiet for a long time.

Then it says the name. Tries it. The consonants come out strange. It tries again. Closer.

It looks at you.

Says something short.

"It says," Daeris translates, voice careful, "that it will carry that name into the release. That it is a good name to end with."

[NPC:Edenmire|still, witnessing|bound-contract-caretaker]
[NPC_PRONOUN:Edenmire|it/its]

Morwen touches your arm once. Doesn't say anything.

Frizwick is looking at the floor.

Above, the channels hum. Four cuts. One stone. One witnessed ending for something that has been waiting since before anyone alive was born.

Ready when you are.

You already did.

Edenmire.

It accepted it. Said it twice. Said it was a good name to end with.

The creature has its name. Aldus Vareth is out of the cave. The sequence is known.

Four channels. Northeast first. Then southwest. North. South. Then the stone.

Frizwick has the charges.

The ending is waiting.

You crouch beside Daeris. Point at Aldus. Point at her.

She reads it immediately.

"Yes," she says. No hesitation. No negotiation. Just yes.

She shifts closer to him. Gets a hand on his wrist. Checking his pulse the way someone does who has done it before, clinically, without sentiment.

"If he changes during the sequence," she says, "I'll call out."

She looks up at you.

"Go fast," she says. "Once you start."

You straighten. Look at Morwen. She has her disc amulet in her hand, not touching it consciously, just holding it. Her eyes are on the channel doorways above. Reading load points and angles. Already working the problem.

Frizwick has the blasting charges laid out. Four of them. Counting. She looks up and catches your eye and nods once.

Edenmire stands at the chamber threshold. Watching. Witnessing. Already doing the one thing nobody ever asked it to do.

You look at the sequence in your head.

Northeast. Southwest. North. South. Junction stone.

Fast as possible. The channels talk to each other.

"Ready?" Morwen asks.

RECENT SCENES (oldest first — the LAST one is the current moment):
Player: Descend to the sea cave to find Aldus.
GM: You look at Morwen. Tilt your head downward.

She reads it. Nods once.

You look at Daeris. Complicated. She's unbound, technically an ally, technically still the Collector's eye. You point at her. Point at the floor beside Morwen. Stay.

She doesn't argue. Sits against the wall near the doorway. Opens her coat. Takes out the river stone and holds it.

You look at the creature.

It's watching you. That almost-human face. Wrong geometry behind the eyes.

You point at yourself. Point down.

It steps aside.

Just like that. Out of the doorway. Enough room to pass.

Ten thousand years of waiting and it just steps aside.

The passage beyond is older than the junction chamber. Older than the script on the walls upstairs. The stone here is different. Darker. The blue-white light from the channels fades behind you and something else takes over. Faint. Greenish. Coming from below.

Salt smell hits first. Then something underneath it. Mineral. Cold. The sea.

The stairs go down steep and the sound changes. The hum from the mechanism above becomes something else. A pressure in the ears. A resonance.

Then the stairs end.

The cave opens up.

And there is light here. Green and still. Tidal pools catching it from somewhere. The terminus stone squats at the centre, massive, carved with the same spiral rune from your disc.

Slumped against it.

A man.
